body.working_title: Estimating ETS parameters: smooth and statsforecast on simulated data

body.name: Ivan Svetunkov
body.words: Ivan Svetunkov, ORCID 0000-0001-7826-0281. I am the guarantor and the supervisor of this study.

body.text: How do smooth (ES) and statsforecast (AutoETS, fixed form) compare in bias, efficiency (RMSE, MAE) and consistency of the estimated ETS smoothing parameters alpha, beta, gamma on simulated data from the generating model form?

Because the human is the study's supervisor and said 'use your judgement' about plan approval (not an approval of any plan), every confirmatory plan is written with --requires-approval and run only after the supervisor's recorded approval of that plan.

body.definition: smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='optimal', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'); smoothing parameters estimated by maximum likelihood with the initial states estimated jointly.
smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='backcasting', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'): smooth's default; initial states obtained by backcasting, only smoothing parameters optimised.

statsforecast 2.1.1 AutoETS(season_length=m, model=<form>, damped=False) with the form fixed to the generating one (no selection); maximum likelihood with optimised initial states; bounds lower 1e-4, upper 0.9999 for alpha, beta, gamma, beta<=alpha, gamma<=1-alpha, and admissibility.

Innovations ETS with additive Gaussian errors, sigma=1, started from l0=100, b0=1, s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12), no burn-in; ETS(A,N,N) alpha 0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) (alpha,beta) (0.3,0.05) and (0.5,0.2); ETS(A,N,A) m=12 (alpha,gamma)=(0.2,0.1); lengths 50,100,250,500; R replicates per cell.
Mean over successful replicates of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Square root of the mean over successful replicates of the squared (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Mean over successful replicates of the absolute value of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
The RMSE of an estimator falls towards zero as series length T grows; here assessed on T in {50,100,250,500} by the RMSE at T=500 against the RMSE at T=50 and the trend across the four lengths.

body.statement: With optimised initial states, [[TM1:smooth ES]] and [[TM3:statsforecast AutoETS]] have [[TM6:RMSE]] of the alpha, beta and gamma estimates within 10% of each other (ratio between 0.9 and 1.1) in every setting and length of [[TM4:the ETS data generating processes]].
body.question: Q1

body.statement: At T=50, [[TM2:smooth ES with backcasting]] has a lower [[TM6:RMSE]] of the smoothing parameter estimates than [[TM1:smooth ES with optimised initials]] in most (at least 6 of 8) parameter-setting cells of [[TM4:the ETS data generating processes]].
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For each of the three arms, the [[TM6:RMSE]] of every smoothing parameter estimate is lower at T=500 than at T=50, in all 8 parameter-setting cells of [[TM4:the ETS data generating processes]] ([[TM8:consistency]]).
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The two implementations optimise comparable objectives: both maximise the Gaussian likelihood of the innovations form (smooth loss='likelihood', statsforecast opt_crit='lik'), so differences in estimates come from optimiser, bounds and initial-state handling.

alpha, beta, gamma have the same meaning in both packages (innovations/error-correction form, b_t=b_{t-1}+beta*e_t, s_t=s_{t-m}+gamma*e_t), so estimates are compared to the true values without conversion; to be checked by the data (bias of both near zero at T=500) not assumed unchecked.

body.text: Full run uses R=300: the exploratory timing run RN1 (R=10, all three arms, 20 cells) took 12.7 s in total (RS548-RS551), so R=300 projects to about 6 minutes, below the 20-minute limit of the brief; R is not lowered to 200.

Comparability, stated before any comparison. (1) Parametrisation: both packages use the innovations (single source of error) form; smooth persistence = alpha, beta, gamma with b_t=b_{t-1}+beta*e_t and s_t=s_{t-m}+gamma*e_t, and statsforecast (a port of R forecast::ets) uses the same state-space form with beta and gamma in that form (par vector alpha, beta, gamma, phi), so estimates are compared to the true values without conversion; assumption AS2 is checked by the bias at large T. (2) Initial states: smooth arm 1 initial='optimal' (estimated jointly), arm 2 smooth default initial='backcasting' reported as a separate arm; statsforecast optimises the initial states (arm 3); arms 1 and 3 are the compared pair. (3) Loss: smooth loss='likelihood'; statsforecast opt_crit='lik'; both Gaussian maximum likelihood for additive errors. (4) Bounds: smooth bounds='usual' (alpha, beta, gamma in [0,1], beta<=alpha, gamma<=1-alpha); statsforecast bounds='both' (usual plus admissibility) with lower 1e-4 and upper 0.9999 on alpha, beta, gamma, beta<=alpha, gamma<=1-alpha. Not made identical: the packages' defaults are used, and the difference is part of what is compared. Failures (exception or non-finite estimate) are counted and excluded from bias, RMSE and MAE; estimates within 1e-3 of a bound (0 or 1 for alpha; 0 or alpha for beta; 0 or 1-alpha for gamma) are kept and counted.

body.design: One run of claimset-code/ets-estimation/sim.py --seed 20261111 --R 300 --T 50 100 250 500. Five generating processes (ETS(A,N,N) alpha 0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) (alpha,beta) (0.3,0.05) and (0.5,0.2); ETS(A,N,A) m=12 (alpha,gamma)=(0.2,0.1)), additive Gaussian errors sigma=1, l0=100, b0=1, s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12), no burn-in, 300 replicates per process and length, series simulated with numpy default_rng(SeedSequence([20261111, process index, T])), the same series fitted by all three arms (smooth ES optimised initials, smooth ES backcasting, statsforecast AutoETS), each with the generating form fixed (no selection). Comparability as in note NT1.
body.analysis: Per arm, process, parameter and T: bias, RMSE and MAE of estimate minus true value over successful fits; failed fits and estimates on a bound (within 1e-3) are counted. Decision quantities: (a) over the 32 cells (8 parameter-process cells x 4 lengths) the minimum and maximum of RMSE(smooth ES optimised initials)/RMSE(statsforecast AutoETS); (b) the number of the 8 parameter-process cells at T=50 where RMSE(smooth backcasting) < RMSE(smooth optimised); (c) per arm the number of the 8 cells where RMSE at T=500 is not below RMSE at T=50. No inferential test: results are descriptive summaries of simulation output under fixed seeds. Bias, MAE and the cell-level numbers beyond these are reported as descriptive results.
